articleTitle: Throughput Prediction Using LS-SVM For 4g-LTE Network and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence(AI) with Long-Term Evolution (LTE) networks offers substantial potential for improving communication infrastructure. By harnessing AI algorithms, it is possible to dynamically optimize network parameters, proactively predict and mitigate equipment failures, and enhance Quality of Service (QoS) by prioritizing critical services through real-time analysis of key performance indicators. This study focuses on predicting network throughput using Least Square Support Vector Machine (LS-SVM). The predictive models developed can trigger adaptive network reconfigurations, ensuring that the network responds promptly to changing conditions. Simulation results reveal that the integration of LS-SVM significantly improves prediction accuracy, enabling more effective implementation of self-organizing network strategies in real-time.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Beam-Steering Metamaterial Lens for 5G and Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper presents an AI-driven metamaterial-based transmissive lens for 5G and autonomous vehicle applications. A genetic algorithm (GA) model is used to design and optimize unit cells, achieving precise phase control through the integration of two PIN diodes. The unit cell design is optimized to ensure high transmission coefficients and a 180° phase shift difference between the diode states. Furthermore, an extended AI-based framework leverages real-time sensor data from autonomous vehicles to dynamically control beam steering using machine learning (ML) models. Full-wave simulations validate the performance of this system, demonstrating beam steering at different angles from 0 to 45 degrees. This capability can be extended to enable wider 2D beam scanning, showcasing enhanced functionality for real-world autonomous applications.

articleTitle: Real-Time Obstacle Detection and Path Adjustment for Autonomous Robots Using OpenCV
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The real-time obstacle detection and path adjustment system for autonomous robots presented in this paper was created using OpenCV. The combination of image processing techniques enables the robot to identify and navigate around any obstacle efficiently. The main functions include real-time image acquisition; where the robot constantly takes pictures of its surroundings, and obstacle detection; which uses edge detection and contour analysis for proper identification of hazards in the environment. The method entails that once an object is detected, the robot's route is reshaped with sophisticated algorithms that are aimed at optimizing navigation as well as minimizing collision probabilities. A wide range of challenging settings such as static or dynamic environments were subjected to rigorous testing on the proposed system. The results indicate that it is robust and effective in detecting obstacles reliably to enhance navigation based on its capacity to make adjustments during operation time (discovered employing experimentation that took place in these settings).

articleTitle: Backward Design with Machine Learning: A Comparative Study for Predicting Electrical Width of Square Ring Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The production of antennas involves several stages, notably the design phase, which must adhere to specific requirements. This process demands extensive testing and measurements. Engineers often use two methods: post-production benchmarking, which is costly, or full-wave electromagnetic simulation software, which is time-consuming. The forward design approach involves setting a target value for a specific trait, such as frequency, and then trying different geometries until the most suitable one is found to meet the goal requirements. An emerging approach, gaining interest due to advances in machine learning, is backward design. In backward design, we start with the goal and use predictive models to determine the geometry that will achieve the desired outcome. Where machine learning (ML) is leveraged to predict the optimal antenna geometry for a desired frequency, bypassing the need to measure multiple antenna traits. This paper explores the comparison of tree models, neural networks, Support Vector Machines (SVM), ensemble models, and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) models, eliminating the weakest models at different stages of the comparison. Comparative analysis of these models encompasses mean square error (MSE), as well as prediction score (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). This research contributes four main sections elucidating the methodology, experimental setup, and results analysis, underscoring the efficacy of our machine learning approach in antenna optimization. The achieved R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score, which falls within the range of 0.99976, is exceptionally close to unity. Such a high R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score signifies a high degree of correlation between the model's predictions and the actual values, indicating outstanding predictive performance.

articleTitle: ADAN-Driven Tuberculosis Diagnosis: A Deep Learning Approach for Chest X-Rays
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Recent advancements in medical imaging and deep learning have shown promise in the accurate identification of lung abnormalities, particularly Tuberculosis, through chest radiography. This paper proposed a new classification method for distinguishing between Tuberculosis and Normal chest X-rays, addressing imbalanced data challenges using the Adaptive Data Augmentation Network (ADAN) strategy during training. Using the Tuberculosis Chest X-ray dataset, the study used a modified ResNet50V2 feature extractor, followed by global pooling and multilayer perception techniques for classification. Through intelligent hyperparameter tuning facilitated by ADAN, the proposed method achieved a maximum accuracy of 0.98, with a recall of 1.00 for the normal class and 0.91 for the tuberculosis class. Furthermore, the study identified the impacting factors of the method based on obtained results, highlighting the significance of ADAN, feature extraction, and classification phases. The proposed method exhibits promising results, aiming to improve the detection rate of tuberculosis and expedite the diagnostic process.

articleTitle: A Novel Cluster Head Selection Algorithm Based on Q-Learning for Internet of Things Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative solution for real-time data collection in the Internet of Things (IoT). Our research focuses on optimizing data collection in IoT networks through the development of a reinforcement learning-based algorithm that efficiently structures the network. Specifically, we propose a novel method utilizing Q-learning to optimize routing in IoT by dynamically selecting an optimal set of Cluster Heads (CHs). The reward function is carefully designed to achieve multiple objectives: increasing network throughput, improving CH dispersion, minimizing the energy consumption of network nodes and CH nodes, reducing the standard deviation of energy consumption among CH nodes, mitigating message loss from CH failures, and decreasing transmission delays. These enhancements contribute to the resilience, efficiency, and overall performance of IoT networks.

articleTitle: Date Fruit Classification Using Transfer Learning: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Dates are one of the most popular and consumed fruits in North Africa, with millions of tons produced annually. Dates are an important part of diets because they are full of vital vitamins and minerals and have a high nutritional value. This fruit contains many different varieties, which the identification and classification plays a crucial role in agriculture. Our study proposes to classify 10 Algerian date by employing three pretrained convolutional neural network models: VGG16, MobileNetV1, and InceptionV3. Among these models, MobileNetV1 achieved the highest test accuracy, at 96.02%, while VGG16 and InceptionV3 attained accuracy rates of 95.45% and 94.32%, respectively. This model's efficacy in identifying date varieties helps farmers by offering an accurate tool for improving date sorting and quality control, hence benefiting agricultural management and market value.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of MDM Fibers Using a Tunable Difference of Gaussian (DoG) Profile for Robust Cylindrical Vector Mode Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Mode-division multiplexing (MDM) using fiber cylindrical vector (CV) modes holds significant potential for enhancing optical communication capacity. However, designing fibers that effectively guide and separate CV modes with optimized performances remains challenging. This work presents a novel MDM fiber based on the Difference of Gaussian (DoG) function. It incorporates four tunable shape parameters to guide robust CV modes. The design trade-offs and performance metrics of the proposed DoG fiber are numerically investigated. The results demonstrate that the fiber supports CV modes with high modal separation (∆n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf> > 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>), indicating minimal channel crosstalk across the C+L ITU-T bands. Furthermore, the guided CV channels exhibit low differential group delays (DGD) and chromatic dispersion (CD), making the DoG fiber an excellent candidate for optical communication systems and/or other applications involving CV mode transmission through fibers.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of 5G Patch Antenna at 28 GHz by Metamaterial Superstrate Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper explores the performance enhancement of a patch antenna by integrating a dual triangular split-ring resonator (DT-SRR) metamaterial (MTM)superstrate designed using CST 2024. The superstrate operates at 28 GHz in the 5G millimeter-wave frequency band. It is simulated to leverage double-negative (DNG) metamaterial properties to improve the antenna system’s gain and bandwidth characteristics. Simulation findings indicate that the antenna’s gain increases from 8.4 dB to 11.4 dB while the impedance bandwidth expands from 2.3 GHz to 3.4 GHz. These findings highlight the potential of the proposed design for enhancing performance in 5G millimeter-wave communication applications.

articleTitle: Cutting-Edge ECG Classification Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Precise classification of ECG signals is vital for detecting and managing arrhythmias, ensuring accurate diagnoses, and facilitating tailored treatment approaches. Identifying different types of arrhythmias enables timely intervention and improves patient outcomes. Improved classification methods increase diagnostic accuracy and optimize therapeutic strategies. This study presents a robust method for classifying ECG heartbeats using the MIT–BIH Arrhythmia Database data. We developed a deep 6-layer one–dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) to effectively classify heartbeat segments such as Normal (N), Left Bundle Branch Block (LBBB), Right Bundle Branch Block (RBBB), Atrial Premature Contraction (APC), and Premature Ventricular Contraction (PVC). The methodology involved extracting and preprocessing ECG signals, padding segments to ensure uniform length, and one–hot encoding of labels. The dataset was divided into training and test sets, with 20% reserved for evaluation. The proposed 1D–CNN architecture includes three Conv1D layers followed by three dense layers, with batch normalization and dropout implemented to improve performance and prevent overfitting. The model achieved a test accuracy of 99.11% , a loss of 0.0463, and an AUC of 0.9995, demonstrating its effectiveness in accurately classifying ECG heartbeats. These results validate the model’s suitability for practical applications in arrhythmia detection and monitoring, highlighting its potential for real-time cardiovascular health monitoring and diagnostic support.

articleTitle: Enhancing Wireless Power Transfer Efficiency by Improving Transmitting Antenna Gain for Implantable Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This study presents a near-field wireless power transfer (WPT) system specifically designed for implantable medical devices, the system operates at 2.42 GHz within the medical implant communication service (MICS) band and employs a coplanar waveguide (CPW) antenna as the external transmitter. This antenna is distinguished by its flexibility, providing a reliable and efficient means of communication with implanted devices while ensuring high power transfer efficiency. To further enhance the antenna’s performance, a reflector was installed behind it to improve directivity and optimize power transfer to the receiver, which was implanted in a simulated environment using a three-layer box. Simulated results demonstrate that the presence of the reflector significantly enhances the effectiveness of the WPT link, highlighting its strong Power transfer efficiency (PTE). This research represents the impact of the transmitting antenna’s gain in WPT technology for implantable medical devices.

articleTitle: IRS-Aided Wireless Systems: Outage and Ergodic Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This work investigates the performance of an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-enabled network under Nakagami-m fading conditions. The outage probability (OP) is approximated using the central limit theorem (CLT) and the second-order moment matching method, while the ergodic capacity (EC) is analyzed based on the results from the CLT approximation. To examine the impact of several parameters on the system’s performance, Monte Carlo simulations’ results disclose the significant influence of the parameters under study on the system’s OP and EC.

articleTitle: Enhancing CFAR Detection Performance In Pareto Distributed Radar Clutter Using Product of Ranked Data Ratios
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: In this conference paper, a new ranked data CFAR detector acting over a clutter following a Pareto distribution is developed. This detector, called PQRS-CFAR, is mainly based on the product of quotients of any two consecutively ranked samples within the detection window, hence the abbreviation PQRS. It is designed to work effectively in more realistic environments, where prior information about clutter parameters is no longer required. This makes it more suitable for practical scenarios. The authors provide here a semi-complete performance study of the proposed detection scheme in uniform clutter and in the presence of interferers within the sample window. Under uniform clutter assumption, an exact analytical expression for the false alarm probability of the introduced PQRS-CFAR is provided as well. The capabilities of the PQRS-CFAR detections are explored and evaluated against a number of existing CFAR competitors via numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cochlear Implant Signal Coding with Scaled Dot-Product Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Cochlear implants (CIs) play a vital role in restoring hearing for individuals with severe to profound sensorineural hearing loss by directly stimulating the auditory nerve with electrical signals. While traditional coding strategies, such as the advanced combination encoder (ACE), have proven effective, they are constrained by their adaptability and precision. This paper investigates the use of deep learning (DL) techniques to generate electrodograms for CIs, presenting our model as an advanced alternative. We compared the performance of our model with the ACE strategy by evaluating the intelligibility of reconstructed audio signals using the short-time objective intelligibility (STOI) metric. The results indicate that our model achieves a STOI score of 0.6031, closely approximating the 0.6126 score of the ACE strategy, and offers potential advantages in flexibility and adaptability. This study underscores the benefits of incorporating artificial intelligent (AI) into CI technology, such as enhanced personalization and efficiency.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Flexible Architecture for Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative dual-mode architecture for DCT and Sobel edge detection, optimized to require only 14 additions. The scalable architecture supports larger word lengths and was successfully implemented on a Xilinx Virtex-V FPGA using VHDL. The implementation demonstrates significant advantages, including reduced FPGA logic area comparable architectures, all at a higher clock frequency. The design shows strong potential for scalability and integration with similar modules. Overall, the proposed architecture enhances both performance and complexity, offering a robust solution for real-time image encoding and edge detection applications.

articleTitle: Packet Delivery Ratio Assessment and Analysis of OLSR Protocol for FANETs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This study explores Flying Ad Hoc Networks (FANETs) comprised of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), which play a vital role in applications such as aerial surveillance, disaster response, and environmental monitoring. A notable challenge associated with the Optimized Link State Routing (OLSR) protocol is packet loss, an issue that arises from its proactive nature. While this characteristic ensures low end-to-end delay making OLSR advantageous in critical situations, it can adversely affect overall reliability. Utilizing the NS-2.35 simulator, this research evaluates the performance of OLSR by analyzing how various factors, such as operational area size, mobility models, node speed, and traffic rate, impact the Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR). Several mobility models, including time, random and group-based movements, are employed to simulate realistic UAV behaviors. The study underscores OLSR’s robustness in these contexts, particularly noting that the Pursue Mobility Model (PMM) is particularly effective in sustaining a high PDR. Moreover, the findings emphasize the significant impact of area size on OLSR’s performance, providing valuable insights for optimizing FANET deployments and enhancing the reliability and efficiency of these systems in critical applications.

articleTitle: Fast Convergence and Low Complexity Algorithm for Multichannel Adaptive Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: In this research, we propose a new multi-channel adaptive filtering method with low complexity and optimized convergence rate. The basic strategy behind the proposed algorithm is to generalize the decorrelation technique used in FNLMS algorithm to the multi-channel case by estimating the prediction parameters for each channel to decorrelate the multi-channel input signals. In simulation we confirm the high performances of the proposed algorithm with comparison of the two dimensions multi-channel Affine Projection (multi-channel APA) and the multi-channel Normalized Least Mean Square (multi-channel NLMS) algorithms.

articleTitle: A New Chaotic System Based on 1D-Enhanced Logistic Map for Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper presents an improved chaotic version of the Enhanced Logistic Map (ELM), which exhibits an expanded chaotic range and significantly enhanced chaotic properties compared to the classic logistic map. This new version offers promising potential for various cryptographic applications. To demonstrate its practical value, we propose a simple yet effective image encryption scheme that leverages the chaotic behavior of ELM. The scheme focuses on efficiently permuting image pixel locations and values, resulting in quick encryption and decryption processes. Comprehensive security analyses and simulation results have been conducted, which confirm that the proposed encryption scheme provides robust protection for images. Furthermore, it demonstrates high resistance to various known cryptographic attacks, making it a reliable solution for securing sensitive image data with minimal computational overhead.

articleTitle: Effects of physical and geometrical properties on the bandgap of photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: In this research, we investigate the effects of shape, physical properties, and material types of photonic crystals (PCs) structure on their photonic bandgap (PBG). A PC structure is designed with 26×26 holes embedded in a slab in two different shapes: hexagonal and square. We also studied the material type utilized for designing the photonic crystal slab of the hexagonal and square structures. To achieve this, gallium arsenide (GaAs), silicon (Si), and germanium (Ge) materials are used as the slab to design the hexagonal and square-connected PCs structures containing a group of holes made from the air. To calculate the photonic band gap (PBG) of the proposed structures, the plane wave expansion method is applied. As a result, we have found a PBG with an average around the band of telecommunication at 1550 nm, with the hexagonal connected structure using the silicon material for a =480 nm, r =228.5 nm, and FF =0.46.

articleTitle: Type-2 Fuzzy Controller for Path Tracking of a Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This study introduces a Type-2 fuzzy logic control (FLC) approach for precise trajectory tracking of mobile robots, emphasizing its superiority in handling complex paths. Using a kinematic model, the proposed Type-2 FLC relies on expert knowledge to reduce tracking errors by adjusting robot movement based on calculated distance and angular discrepancies from the desired trajectory. The enhanced Type-2 fuzzy controller demonstrates significant accuracy and robustness, especially in challenging tracking scenarios, showcasing notable improvements in error reduction and control smoothness. Simulation results confirm that the proposed approach outperforms other methods, highlighting its potential for applications requiring reliable and precise navigation.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an IoT-Driven Irrigation System with Solar Power and Real-Time Remote Monitoring for Sustainable Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The use of IoT technology in irrigation systems plays a crucial role in agriculture by enabling precise monitoring and control of water resources. This paper presents the design and implementation of a sustainable IoT-based irrigation system utilizing GPRS for remote monitoring. The system integrates ESP32 and LilyGO T-Call SIM800L microcontrollers to collect environmental data such as soil moisture, humidity, and temperature, which is processed and visualized on the Thing Speak platform. Solar energy powers the system, ensuring continuous operation in remote areas with minimal human intervention, and its low-cost design makes it suitable for large agricultural areas. Mesh communication enhances network reliability, enabling decentralized data flow between nodes, while the small solar panels offer a clean energy solution with extended battery life, allowing each sensor node to operate for up to 47 days without solar charging. The system facilitates efficient water management by activating irrigation based on real-time environmental conditions, thus conserving resources and improving crop yields. Additionally, the system has the potential to monitor and manage large-scale irrigation in real-time and could be integrated within the irrigation chain for remote operation. The proposed solution showcases the potential of IoT to promote water conservation and improve agricultural productivity sustainably.

articleTitle: Analytical Investigation of Compact Square-Ring Antenna Printed on Anisotropic Substances
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a square-ring compact microstrip antenna on a uniaxial anisotropic substrate. We explore the advantages of this design, focusing on its compact size and enhanced performance compared to traditional configurations. A modified cavity model is utilized for the analysis. The numerical data shows the primary attributes of the antenna, like its resonant frequency, we conduct a parametric study to analyze the effect of the key parameters, including substrate material and thickness, for improved resonant frequency. Our results demonstrate the potential of uniaxial anisotropic substrates in achieving higher performance for compact antennas.

articleTitle: Enhanced Bearing Fault Diagnosis Using Transfer Learning and Spectrograms with Pretrained GoogLeNet
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of modern machinery, there is a rising demand for advanced intelligent algorithms capable of diagnosing faults in rotating equipment through vibration signal analysis. In response, we introduce a fault diagnosis method based on transfer learning, utilizing a pretrained GoogLeNet model and spectrogram representations generated from vibration signals. By using the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) bearing dataset, raw vibration data is converted into spectrograms to capture the time-frequency attributes of the signals. These spectrograms are then input into the pretrained GoogLeNet, which was originally developed for large-scale image recognition, to extract deep features crucial for fault detection. Through transfer learning, the model leverages the pretrained network’s ability to recognize complex patterns, significantly improving fault classification accuracy while minimizing the need for extensive labeled data and training time. Experimental results confirm that our approach surpasses traditional methods, delivering enhanced diagnostic performance on the CWRU dataset. This research underscores the effectiveness of applying pretrained convolutional neural networks combined with spectrograms for accurate and efficient machinery fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Antenna Design for Millimeter-Wave Systems: A Comprehensive Literature Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Research on reconfigurable antennas is crucial for smart and adaptive systems due to their multi-functionality, compact size, reduced processing, strong isolation, and out-of-band rejection. These antennas are ideal for wireless applications like fourth-generation (4G) and fifth-generation (5G) mobile terminals. Active materials like MEMS, varactor diodes, and PIN diodes can modify antenna propertie. Research is particularly focused on Millimeter-waves (mmWave) bands, which offer high data rates and bandwidth.

articleTitle: Synthesis of a Tri-Band Microstrip Patch Antenna Using Genetic Algorithm for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The low-profile nature of microstrip antennas is highly convenient for many mm-wave wireless applications; however, they typically resonate at a single frequency with limited directivity and narrow bandwidth. This article explores patch antenna geometry optimization to achieve tri-band frequency operation with improved working bandwidth and directivity by employing a binary-coded genetic algorithm. The algorithm constantly creates new geometry to search for the fittest individual on the patch surface until the termination criteria are fulfilled. The optimized antenna is simulated using ANSYS HFSS software and compared to the reference antenna as well as with other related works in the literature. The results show that the optimized antenna resonates at 28.0 GHz, 38.73 GHz, and 60.48 GHz with a peak directivity of 6.72 dB, 7.66 dB, and 8.49 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: A simple compact Microstrip Patch Antenna with optimized performance for 5G Wireless Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a simple compact microstrip patch antenna optimized for 5G wireless communication. The antenna design employs the RT/duroid® 5880 substrate, which has a low dielectric constant of 2.2 and a minimal loss tangent of 0.0009, making it suitable for high-performance applications. The simulated antenna measures 6 × 6 × 0.508 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The results demonstrate that the antenna is appropriate for 5G applications, featuring a bandwidth of 940 MHz centered at 28 GHz and a high gain of 5.35 dBi, making it practical for use in dense urban environments. The directional radiation pattern enhances performance in high-frequency 5G networks, while the compact design facilitates the miniaturization required for next-generation wireless devices. This study contributes to advancing efficient, high-performance antenna solutions essential for reliable 5G network deployment.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient Wireless Power Transfer Systems for Implantable Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This study introduces a near-field wireless power transfer (WPT) system tailored for medical implants. The system operates at 2.42 GHz in the medical implantable communication service (MICS) band and employs a simple patch antenna as the external transmitter. A key feature of the system is its compact receiver antenna measuring 6.8 mm × 6.5 mm × 0.5 mm. and a total volume of 22.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, making it suitable for implantation. The performance of the WPT link was evaluated by implanting the receiver in a three-layer tissue model. Simulation results demonstrate the proposed WPT system’s ability to achieve high power transfer efficiency (PTE). This research also investigates how the distance between the transmitter and receiver antennas affects WPT technology for implantable medical devices, emphasizing the need to maintain optimal spacing to ensure reliable power delivery and enhance the performance of these vital medical devices, thereby contributing to advancements in healthcare.

articleTitle: Triple-band Antenna Dielectric Resonator-based for Millimeter-wave and Sub-6 Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The paper presents a novel triple-band dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) tailored for millimeter-wave (mm-wave) and microwave GHz applications. The design features three main elements: a cylindrical dielectric resonator (CDR) for the mm-wave range, activated by a slot in the ground, and two ring-shaped dielectric resonators (RDRs) for the Sub-6 GHz range, each powered by vertical microstrip lines. Low-pass filters (LPFs) are embedded in each RDR to suppress undesirable resonances in the mm-wave band. The CDR is fine-tuned for 28 GHz operation, reaching a gain of 17.8 dBi and a bandwidth of 17.3%. The larger RDR operates at 2.4 GHz, delivering a gain of 7.5 dBi and a bandwidth of 26.9%, while the smaller RDR functions at 5.2 GHz, with a gain of 5.3 dBi and a bandwidth of 17.2%. The antenna demonstrates outstanding isolation, surpassing 30 dB in all bands, making it an ideal candidate for 5G systems.

articleTitle: Alzheimer’s Disease Detection using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Alzheimer’s Disease is a progressive and irreversible neurodegenerative disorder. Being the most common cause of dementia, it affects millions of people around the world, making early detection and diagnosis a necessity. Deep learning can help detect the numerous patterns associated with this disease, aiding in its early diagnosis. This work uses a transfer learning approach to classify MRI images into Alzheimer’s Disease, Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), and Cognitively Normal (CN) classes by leveraging VGG16 and VGG19 models pre-trained on ImageNet. The dataset used for training is acquired from the ADNI dataset, down-sampled and up-sampled to mitigate the class imbalance issue. This approach yielded high accuracy rates ranging from 98.14% to 99.59%.

articleTitle: A Dilated CNN and BiLSTM-GRU Based on Multi-Noise Classifier for Single Speech enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: In this study, we propose a new acoustic noise reduction system based on deep learning. To enhance speech quality n many fields such as medical, mobile telephony and free-hand applications, various techniques, including adaptive filtering, have been utilized. Advances in AI research and data availability have been leveraged in many recent works to enhance speech and reduce acoustic noise. In this paper, we propose a novel two-stage noise reduction system. Our system includes a BiLSTM-based classification model to identify the type of noise, followed by several noise reduction models based on dilated Inception CNNs and another architecture based on BiLSTM-GRU. The system was evaluated using both objective metrics, such as PESQ and STOI, and subjective listening tests. Our proposed ID-CNN model achieved a PESQ score of 2.23 and a STOI score of 85% for Babble noise, outperforming the baseline HSD model by 18%. Additionally, the model significantly improved performance for babble, car, and engine noises, demonstrating robust noise reduction across a wide range of environments

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Automatic Text Summarization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: In today's digital age, the rapid accumulation of textual information necessitates effective automatic text summarization. The demand for computer systems capable of summarizing vast amounts of information has grown exponentially, aiding users in extracting key insights and making informed decisions. This study focuses on the development of a robust abstractive text summarization model utilizing Deep Learning and Seq2Seq models with LSTM networks and attention mechanisms. Through the construction of a Seq2Seq-based framework incorporating LSTM layers and attention mechanisms, the model effectively captures semantic relationships and contextual dependencies within the input text. Training strategies, optimization techniques, and word embedding methods, including pretrained word embedding like GloVe, were employed to enhance the model's ability to generate accurate and concise summaries.

articleTitle: A Novel High-gain Vivaldi Antenna for Millimeter-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a novel fomre Vivaldi antenna for 5G applications. With the rapid growth of 5G technology, antennas capable of supporting high-frequency operations, wide bandwidth, and enhanced gain are essential. The proposed Vivaldi antenna operates in the millimeter-wave frequency range, specifically optimized for 5G communication bands. Key design features include a tapered slot structure and dielectric loading to improve impedance matching and radiation efficiency. Over the intended frequency range, the antenna achieves a wide bandwidth, good directivity, and a consistent emission pattern. The antenna is appropriate for incorporation into 5G base stations with good performance in terms of return loss, VSWR, and radiation characteristics, as shown by extensive simulations and testing. This antenna’s broadband characteristics, small size, and high gain make it a viable option for next high-speed wireless communication systems. The antenna is designed, simulated, and analyzed by using computer simulation technology microwave studio (CST-MWS), and we achieved a very good matching among the results.

articleTitle: Simulated Annealing-Based Design for Hybrid Digital and Analog Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Hybrid analog and digital beamforming is an efficient solution for large-scale antenna systems, offering reduced costs, complexity, and power consumption compared to fully digital beamforming. This study introduces a hybrid beamforming design that achieves comparable performance with fewer RF chains, aligning the RF chain count with the number of data streams to optimize system efficiency. Using simulated annealing, the proposed approach computes analog and digital precoders and combiners in a point-to-point MIMO setting. This optimization method allows for balancing system complexity, cost, and performance by adjusting the number of antennas, RF chains, and data streams. The result demonstrate that increasing antenna count boosts signal quality and system capacity, while a reduced number of RF chains effectively lowers costs without sacrificing performance.

articleTitle: Frequency Reconfigurable Leaky Wave Antenna Design for C-band With Two Slots Based on SIW Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Rapid advancements in Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) technology are being accompanied by the development of reconfigurable antennas, which can dynamically alter characteristics such frequency, radiation pattern, and polarization. To improve performance in a variety of wireless applications, these antennas use elements such as PIN diodes, which function as fast-response switches to alter conductive routes. At the same time, SIW technology makes it possible for small, high-frequency devices to guide waves efficiently, making integration and production simple. When combined, these developments result in telecommunications networks with high-performance, reasonably priced solutions.In this study, we used CST Commercial Studio to design a new leaky wave antenna operating in the C band, based on the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> microwave SIW technology. The suggested antenna is made up of two rectangular slots that are the same length and breadth and are separated from one another by a D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sl</inf> distance. To change the configuration of the leaky wave antenna, a PIN diode was placed in the center of each slot.PIN diodes function as insulators to halt current flow when in the OFF position, which is why they are employed to control current. When in operation, the antenna is correctly grounded and radiates. Through this procedure, the antenna changes its configuration from one frequency to another without changing its size.Return loss measurements of the reconfigurable antenna revealed scans for frequencies between 04 and 08 GHz.

articleTitle: Computer-Assisted Transcription of Scanned Arabic Handwritting Using ConvNeXt Model and Siamese Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The transcription of Arabic handwritten text still remains one of the major challenges because of the morphological complexity of Arabic writing (cursivity, contains diacritical points, several forms for the same letter, etc.), variations in styles writing and degradation of handwritten documents. This paper presents two new deep-learning based approaches of offline Arabic handwriting recognition, intended for a system of Computer-Assisted Transcription (CAT). The first is applied at character level, using the ConvNeXt model (ConvNeXt-tiny-224). The second contribution uses Siamese networks for the retrieval of similar Parts-of-Arabic-Words (PAW). To experiment with the first method, we used three dataset of Arabic handwritten character images; OIHACDB-28, OIHACDB-40 and AIA9K with recognition rates of 98.75%, 99.37% and 94.97% respectively. For the second contribution, a new dataset of PAW is proposed and constructed from the dataset of AHDB words. The results obtained show the effectiveness of Siamese networks for the similar PAW retrieval in a dataset.

articleTitle: Leveraging Support Vector Machines for Precise Attenuation Prediction in WDM-FSO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Free-Space Optical (FSO) communication systems offer high bandwidth and interference immunity, making them attractive for next-generation networks. However atmospheric conditions significantly impact the performance of FSO systems, where attenuation is significant challenge. This research investigates the application of Support Vector Machines (SVM), a powerful machine learning technique, to accurately predict attenuation in Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) FSO systems. By leveraging OptiSystem simulations to generate extensive datasets, we train and evaluate SVM models to predict attenuation levels based on meteorological parameters. The models’ performance is assessed using ROC curves and confusion matrices to measure their ability to distinguish between high and low attenuation scenarios. The findings of this research provide valuable insights into the effectiveness of SVM for predicting attenuation in WDM-FSO systems, enabling proactive mitigation strategies and enhancing system reliability.

articleTitle: Adversarial attacks for speaker recognition system with FGSM-CNN and FGSM-DNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Adversarial attacks are specifically designed to interfere with models of speaker recognition systems by introducing imperceptible noise into speech signals. This paper explores deep learning-based adversarial attacks targeting speaker recognition systems. We used the x-vector framework and various variants of the FGSM technique applied to convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and deep neural networks (DNNs). We evaluated five attack methods: FGSM, BIM, FGSM-CNN and FGSM-DNN. Performance evaluations of the proposed methods were conducted using the LibriSpeech corpus, focusing on the equalised error rate (EER) measured by two metrics: PLDA and Cosine. The experimental results indicate that the proposed adversarial attack methods offer superior performance in terms of EER compared with the traditional FGSM approach.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Wideband Antenna with Coplanar Waveguide Feed for Implantable Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: In this study ultra-miniaturized broadband antenna optimized for biomedical implant applications, operating within the 2.45 GHz industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) band. The suggested broadband antenna demonstrates a highly compact design, with an ultra-small footprint of just 9.13 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (6 mm × 6 mm × 0.38 mm). This minimization is achieved by leveraging high-permittivity materials for both the substrate and super-strate, combined with strategically placed rectangular slotted on the patch. The antenna delivers an impressive broadband performance, covering a frequency interval of 2.1 to 2.62 GHz with a total bandwidth of 520 MHz, making it highly capable of supporting high data rate transmissions. Using a coplanar waveguide (CPW) feeding structure, the antenna achieves a gain of -26.8 dB and exhibits an omnidirectional radiation pattern, enabling reliable data transmission and reception from all directions. These unique features make the antenna exceptionally suited for implantable medical devices, where size, performance, and reliability are critical.

articleTitle: Enhancing Road Safety: Car Crash Detection (CCD) Using CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Due to the severity of car crashes and their significant impact on society and the economy, it has become essential to develop intelligent systems capable of detecting these accidents quickly and accurately. Deep learning and computer vision techniques, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), offer promising possibilities in this field. These networks are characterized by their ability to automatically extract important features from images and videos, making them ideally suited for the task of detecting car crashes. In this study, we propose an innovative model based on CNN for detecting car crashes, with the aim of improving emergency response and reducing the negative impacts of road accidents. The model achieved outstanding results with an Overall Accuracy (OA) of 97.78% and an AUC of 100%, surpassing some previous works in this field. This makes it promising for real-world applications in enhancing road safety systems. It also paves the way for further research and development in this field by integrating more diverse data or exploring advanced deep learning techniques.

articleTitle: Innovative Wireless Solutions for Real-Time ECG Monitoring: Leveraging BLE, Wi-Fi, and LoRa Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The rapid advancement of wireless technologies and the Internet of Things (IoT) has transformed healthcare, enabling real-time monitoring and data transmission for improved patient care. This paper presents an in-depth study of the wireless transmission of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals using Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), Wi-Fi, and Long Range (LoRa) technologies. We explore the architecture, security, energy efficiency, and reliability of each protocol, determining their suitability for healthcare applications. Leveraging IoT integration, we utilize ESP32 and ESP8266 microcontrollers for real-time data transmission to cloud-based platforms, facilitating continuous health monitoring through web and mobile application interfaces. The study also delves into the design and testing of the electrical circuits, incorporating ECG sensors and wireless communication units to establish a robust monitoring system. By automating the collection and analysis of critical health data, the proposed solution enhances diagnostic capabilities, offering flexible and scalable approaches for modern healthcare needs.

articleTitle: Geometric Concept-Driven Blind Source Separation: Comparative Analysis of Analytical and Optimization Methods for Determining Separation Angles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to Blind Source Separation (BSS) for instantaneous linear mixtures, leveraging geometric principles to recover statistically independent source signals. The separation process begins by decorrelating mixed signals to obtain whitened signals, followed by an algorithm that optimally determines rotation angles. We compare three methods: genetic optimization for identifying optimal rotation angles, and two proposed analytical approaches—kurtosis maximization and cross-cumulant minimization. Our comparative analysis demonstrates that effective separation can be achieved by processing each pair of whitened signals independently. Further, a single statistical independence criterion, whether based on kurtosis or cross-cumulants, is sufficient to determine accurate separation angles, resulting in precise and computationally efficient separation, especially compared to genetic optimization.

articleTitle: Neural Network Controller Design for the Path Tracking of a Coaxial Octorotor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper aims to present the design of an angle controller using a neural network for a coaxial octorotor. The neural network design is based on data generated from a fuzzy logic controller, which has demonstrated stability and robustness. The newly designed NN controller will replace two angle controllers that produce pitch and roll momentum, while a neural network controller is also employed for the other subsystems: x, y, yaw, and altitude. The efficiency of the designed controller is tested in the MATLAB Simulink coaxial octorotor 6-DOF (degrees of freedom) dynamic model. The obtained simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the designed controller.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Uncoupled MPTCP Congestion Control Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Multi-Path TCP (MPTCP) extends traditional TCP by enabling simultaneous data transmission over multiple paths, offering potential advantages in terms of throughput and reliability. However, the interaction of MPTCP with various congestion control mechanisms and its behavior under lossy network conditions remain critical areas of investigation. Through this experimentation, we analyze how Cubic and BBR adapt to varying degrees of packet loss and assess their throughput and transfer time characteristics under the same platform. The findings of this study provide valuable insights into the behavior and effectiveness of these algorithms in lossy network conditions, aiding network administrators and protocol designers in making informed decisions for optimizing network performance and reliability.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning-Based Deep Residual Learning for Speech Recognition in Clean and Noisy Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Addressing the detrimental impact of non-stationary environmental noise on automatic speech recognition (ASR) has been a persistent and significant research focus. Despite advancements, this challenge continues to be a major concern. Recently, data-driven supervised approaches, such as deep neural networks, have emerged as promising alternatives to traditional unsupervised methods. With extensive training, these approaches have the potential to overcome the challenges posed by diverse real-life acoustic environments. In this light, this paper introduces a novel neural framework that incorporates a robust frontend into ASR systems in both clean and noisy environments. Utilizing the Aurora-2 speech database, the authors evaluate the effectiveness of an acoustic feature set for Mel-frequency, employing the approach of transfer learning based on Residual neural network (ResNet). The experimental results demonstrate a significant improvement in recognition accuracy compared to convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks. They achieved accuracies of 98.94% in clean and 91.21% in noisy mode.

articleTitle: Review of Multi-Band Shared-Aperture Millimeter-Wave Antennas for Wireless Telecommunications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This review paper offers an extensive analysis of multi-band shared-aperture millimeter-wave antennas, an essential technology for future communication systems. The emphasis is on recent progress in antenna design, showcasing technologies that facilitate efficient operation across various frequency bands utilizing a single aperture. We carefully examine essential methodologies, including frequency-selective surfaces, integrated circuits, and new materials, which enhance performance parameters like as bandwidth, gain, and radiation efficiency. The paper also discusses significant problems, including reducing cross-band interference, maximizing aperture efficiency, and improving spatial selectivity. This study synthesizes current research and technical developments to provide a comprehensive overview of advanced multi-band millimeter-wave antennas and to delineate future research and development trajectories in this swiftly advancing domain.

articleTitle: Two-Channel Forward Set-Membership Normalized Subband Algorithm for Acoustic Noise Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper presents a two-channel forward set-membership normalized subband (TC-F-SM-SB-NLMS) algorithm for acoustic noise reduction. By incorporating set-membership technique, the computational complexity in updating the two cross-filters is reduced, while combining it with subband normalized adaptive filtering ensures high noise reduction performance. The proposed algorithm is compared with the two-channel forward normalized least mean square (TC-F-NLMS), its set-membership variant (TC-F-SM-NLMS), and the two-channel forward subband normalized least mean square (TC-F-SB-NLMS) algorithms. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms these algorithms in terms of computational complexity and segmental signal-to-noise ratio (Seg-SNR) for acoustic noise reduction.

articleTitle: Colorectal Polyp Segmentation Using Modified U-net Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Accurate segmentation of colorectal polyps remains a significant challenge in medical image analysis, yet it is crucial for aiding surgical interventions and preventing colorectal cancer. In this research, we propose a modified U-Net architecture designed to overcome these challenges by enhancing polyp detection and segmentation using colonoscopy medical images. The proposed model integrates deeper layers, add more convolutions layers, and dropout techniques to improve feature extraction and segmentation performance. Tested on the CVC-ClinicDB dataset, the model achieved an accuracy of 99.40%, a Dice coefficient of 97.52%, a precision of 95.69%, and a recall of 99.44%. These results demonstrate the model's potential in addressing segmentation challenges and improving clinical outcomes by providing more accurate segmentation, which can support early diagnosis and precise surgical planning.

articleTitle: Ultrasound Images Classification of Thyroid Cancer using Deep Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The application of computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems in ultrasound (US) image analysis using maching learning (ML) has been widely explored. Recently, deep learning (DL) has played a pivotal role in advancing this research. This paper proposes an automated method for thyroid cancer (TC) image classification, utilizing transfer learning (TL) with VGG16, a well-established pre-trained neural network. The approach involves preprocessing, data augmentation, and classification using TL. The results are compared to convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for distinguishing between benign and malignant thyroid nodules (TNs). Model performance is evaluated using accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score metrics. The promising results highlight the effectiveness of TL in US image analysis. The best results, achieved using the TL algorithm, include an accuracy of 0.9878, sensitivity of 0.9705, specificity of 0.9854, and an F1-score of 0.9866. These values represent significant improvements over the baseline models, and the study is conducted using the DDTI dataset for TC, distinguishing between benign and malignant cases.

articleTitle: Transformer-Based Multi-Head Attention for Noisy Speech Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced transformer-based multi-head attention approach for automatic speech recognition (ASR) in noisy speech environments. The study focuses on four distinct noise scenarios: subway, babble, car, and exhibition hall, each rigorously evaluated across different signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) and a clean condition. Utilizing the AURORA 2 dataset, this research investigates the performance and robustness of the proposed model under these varied acoustic conditions. To further enhance the transformer-based attention’s performance in ASR, we compare its effectiveness against sound classification in environmental noise using the ESC-50 dataset. The experimental results provide a comprehensive analysis, demonstrating that the model with transformer-based multi-head attention, incorporating merging and gammatone frequency cepstral coefficients (GFCC) features, significantly outperforms a baseline model using GFCC features with transformer-based multi-head attention alone, without merging. The model achieves an accuracy of 98.75% on the AURORA 2 dataset in clean conditions, and maintains a high accuracy of 92.38% under noisy conditions. When evaluated on the ESC-10 dataset, it achieves an accuracy of 81.25%, underscoring its robustness and potential for practical deployment in diverse acoustic settings.

articleTitle: Attention Mechanisms with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Detection of Distributed Denial of Service Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: In the constantly evolving landscape of cybersecurity threats, distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks continue to pose a significant challenge, disrupting services and causing substantial economic losses. Conventional detection techniques often struggle with the complexity and magnitude of DDoS attacks, which overwhelm target systems with excessive traffic. Existing methods frequently fail to detect these attacks accurately and promptly, leading to prolonged downtime. This paper proposes a novel solution by integrating Attention mechanisms with deep convolutional networks to enhance DDoS attack detection. The attention layers enable the framework to focus on the most pertinent features in the data, improving its ability to differentiate between normal and malicious traffic. We utilize the comprehensive CIC-IDS2017 dataset to assess our proposed approach. Key performance metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, are employed to evaluate effectiveness. Our experimental results demonstrate that incorporating attention layers significantly enhances detection performance, achieving accuracy and precision rates of over 99.94%. This highlights the potential of our approach to provide a more effective and reliable solution for DDoS attack detection.

articleTitle: An overview of lightpath QoT prediction using machine learning in DWDM Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The work discusses the importance of Quality of Transmission (QoT) in Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM) Networks and how it influences the successful establishment of lightpath connections. It highlights the degradation of QoT caused by physical layer impairments (PLIs) and the need for accurate QoT prediction to guide routing and resource allocation. The paper emphasizes the application of machine learning (ML) models for QoT prediction, given their suitability over traditional analytical models which are challenging to drive and computationally intensive . It presents a summary of QoT prediction strategies in optical networks. Additionally, it outlines ML algorithms, sample data generation. Furthermore, it reviews recent studies on QoT prediction using ML methods and discusses their practical feasibility.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Scheme for PAPR Reduction in FBMC/OQAM Systems-based on Combining Enhanced Companding Transform and TR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: One of the significant challenges in advanced multicarrier communication systems, including those designed for 5G, is the high Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR). This paper addresses the issue of PAPR reduction in Filter Bank Multicarrier with Offset Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (FBMC/OQAM) systems, which are considered a leading candidate for 5G waveform technology. We introduce a hybrid approach that combines an enhanced version of μ-law companding (EMLC) with Tone Reservation (TR) to mitigate PAPR effectively. The performance of the proposed method is assessed through simulations, focusing on the complementary cumulative distribution function (CCDF) of PAPR, bit error rate (BER), and power spectral density (PSD). Our simulation results demonstrate that the hybrid technique significantly lowers PAPR while preserving system performance, making it a viable solution for high-efficiency 5G communication systems.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of SVM and CNN Classifiers for EEG Signal Classification in Response to Different Auditory Stimuli
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This study aims to classify brainwave patterns using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals in response to various auditory stimuli, specifically Quran recitation, participants’ favorite music, and Interstellar’s main theme. By analyzing the unique EEG responses elicited by these stimuli, the study explores cognitive and emotional processing differences. Two prominent classifiers, Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), were utilized. SVM, combined with Power Spectral Density (PSD) features, achieved the highest accuracy of 95% when distinguishing Quran recitation from rest. CNN, particularly with Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) features, exhibited strong performance in distinguishing between different auditory stimuli, with an average accuracy exceeding 90%. These results highlight the critical role of feature extraction techniques, such as PSD and KDE, in improving classification performance and deepening our understanding of EEG-based emotional and cognitive responses to auditory stimuli.

articleTitle: 4G/5G in Smart Cities: Enhanced Analysis for Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Smart cities have recently gained popularity since they improve people’s lives while also ensuring their safety and stability. These cities incorporate a variety of communication technologies, including 4G and 5G networks. This paper presents an in-depth comparison of 4G and 5G technologies in smart cities, with a certain focus on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). We utilize the OMNeT++ simulation platform to analyze the performance of these networks in a highway scenario, examining metrics such as throughput and packet loss. Our simulation results demonstrate that 5G networks achieve up to 60% higher throughput and 40% lower packet loss compared to 4G in highway scenarios with multiple vehicles. These findings suggest that 5G’s enhanced capabilities make it particularly suitable for time-critical ITS applications. Our research not only validates the superior performance of 5G in ITS applications but also provides insights into the challenges and future directions for 5G implementation in smart cities.

articleTitle: Adaptive Cyber-Attack Detection in IIoT Using Attention-Based LSTM-CNN Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The rapid expansion of the industrial Internet of things (IIoT) has introduced new challenges in securing critical infrastructures against sophisticated cyberthreats. This study presents the development and evaluation of an advanced Intrusion detection (IDS) based on a hybrid LSTM-convolution neural network (CNN)-Attention architecture, specifically designed to detect and classify cyberattacks in IIoT environments. The research focuses on two key classification tasks: binary and multi-class classification. The proposed models was rigorously tested using the Edge-IIoTset dataset. To mitigate the class imbalance in the dataset, the synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) was employed to generate synthetic samples for the underrepresented classes. This ensured that the model could learn effectively from all classes, thereby improving the overall classification performance. Through systematic experimentation, various deep learning (DL) models were compared, ultimately demonstrating that the LSTM-CNN-Attention model consistently outperformed others across key performance metrics. In binary classification, the model achieved near-perfect accuracy, while in multi-class classification, it maintained a high accuracy level (99.04%), effectively categorizing different attack types with a loss value of 0.0220%.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology and Smart Contracts for Secure and Thorough Exchange of Health Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The need for increased longevity has led to heightened concern among individuals about aging with quality, resulting in an abundance of wellness and health data. Unfortunately, many of these data are unsuitable for sharing and integration because of their dissimilar structures and semantics, which need to be better utilized and inadequately safeguarded. The existing standards are intricate and require more cooperation from stakeholders to ensure their implementation. Blockchain technology offers a potential solution by providing a unified framework for standards and their implementation through consensus processes that consider the confirmation and confidentiality of data insertion into blocks in the chain. Furthermore, smart contracts can ensure privacy and adherence to protocols that govern data exchange on the blockchain. This study proposes a blockchain structure incorporating a consensus mechanism to accommodate information collected in the wellness and health ecosystem, combining information obtained from IoT devices and stored on middleware platforms. This architecture addresses these challenges and defines the principles for a secure and comprehensive exchange of wellness and health data.

articleTitle: Development of a Deep Learning System for the Prediction of the Reliability of Medicine Boxes in an Industry 4.0 Production line: A Framework for Enhancing Customer Satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Industry 4.0 integrates digital technologies to revolutionize manufacturing, where the reliability of medicine boxes is critical for ensuring product quality and customer safety. This study proposes a deep learning-based quality control system using transfer learning with the VGG16 architecture to assess the reliability of medicine boxes. By classifying boxes as "Good" or "Bad", the proposed model demonstrates high predictive accuracy and minimal loss, showing a strong penitential for real-world application. Key metrics, such as accuracy and F1 score, confirm the robustness of this approach. This system promises to enhance production efficiency, safety, and customer satisfaction, underscoring the role of AI in modern manufacturing.

articleTitle: Enhanced Detection of EVA Discoloration Defects in Solar Cells Using Vision Transformers and Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The aging and degradation of photovoltaic (PV) modules are significantly influenced by various climatic and environmental conditions throughout their operational lifespan. Common defects include discoloration and delamination of encapsulant material, back-sheet bubbling, cell cracks, hot spot-induced cell burning, and anti-reflective coating defects. Traditional detection methods, such as visual inspection and IR thermography, are now being supplemented by advanced AI techniques. In desert installations, discoloration of the ethylenevinyl acetate (EVA) encapsulant is particularly pronounced, resulting from UV radiation, temperatures exceeding 50°C, and exposure to moisture. This study proposes an innovative approach that utilizes automated inspection supported by Vision Transformers and Contrastive Learning to detect PV module defects, with a specific focus on identifying EVA discoloration in polycrystalline modules installed at the Research Unit in Renewable Energies in the Saharan Medium (URERMS) in Adrar.

articleTitle: Water Leak Classification Using Acoustic Data and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Water Distribution Networks (WDNs) are critical infrastructures for delivering potable water from its source to consumers. Unfortunately, these systems often suffer significant water loss from leaks which typically remain undetected until they result in extensive damage. To effectively address these issues there is a pressing need for innovative maintenance strategies that enable early fault detection and rapid response. This paper presents a diagnostic approach that uses acoustic monitoring and Edge-AI techniques to detect failures in urban water pipelines through hydrophone sensor recordings. The methodology employed in this study involves extracting both time-domain and frequency-domain features to classify various pipeline faults using three distinct Machine Learning (ML) models: Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM). Furthermore, we implemented the processing method on an embedded platform, demonstrating its effectiveness in real-world scenarios. The results of this study reveal an average fault detection accuracy of 96.83% with a fast response time of 1.055 seconds.

articleTitle: Enhancing Thyroid Cancer Diagnosis with Advanced Deep Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: The accurate diagnosis of thyroid tumors remains challenging due to their clinical and pathological diversity. This study explores the potential of advanced deep learning models to improve thyroid cancer diagnostics by comparing EfficientNet B4 and MobileNetV3 for histopathological image classification. Both models were fine-tuned using transfer learning on a dataset of 7,272 images, covering Medullary, Papillary, and Vesicular carcinoma types. Performance metrics, including precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy, were used to assess their effectiveness. Findings indicate that both models are highly effective, with EfficientNet B4 exhibiting superior accuracy, particularly in complex diagnostic scenarios. The study also addresses limitations, such as the dataset’s limited size and variability, which may affect model generalization. Ultimately, these advancements in deep learning could significantly enhance thyroid cancer diagnostics, minimize inter-observer variability, and lead to better patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Intelligent Telemedicine System based on Classification and Super Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Conventional telemedicine systems often have problems with image quality, storage space, and transmission speeds. To remedy these problems, we propose an intelligent system that uses advanced image processing techniques. These techniques handle medical scan datasets more efficiently. The proposed system starts by bicubic downsampling images to make them smaller for transmission over channels with limited bandwidth, which speeds up diagnoses. Furthermore, our framework automatically classifies normal and abnormal scans using a deep learning classification model. We enhance abnormal images using a Dynamic Multi-Scale Attention Network (DMSAN), which in turn improve diagnostic clarity significantly. We assess the effectiveness of our telemedicine framework through experiments applied on Chest X-Ray (CXR) scans. The results indicate that our system achieves an impressive 94% accuracy rate in classifying CXR scans. Additionally, the DMSAN outperforms various super-resolution (SR) models in terms of Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) metrics, as well as visual quality. By prioritizing the storage of abnormal scans and ensuring their high quality, our framework optimizes the storage and provides quick management of data that provides clinicians with a valuable tool for rapid and accurate diagnoses, improving patient outcomes in telemedicine.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Graph Autoencoder-based Community Detection in Attributed Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Understanding connections in real-world networks is crucial for optimizing systems. Community detection, powered by techniques such as deep learning, especially Graph Autoencoder (GAE), is designed to learn meaningful graph representations, reveal hidden patterns and key influencers, and enhance network efficiency. This insight aids decision-making across various domains, from social networks to biological systems. In this paper, we begin by proposing a taxonomy of graph autoencoder community detection approaches in attributed networks based on the type of autoencoder: simple or dual encoder. Then, we conduct a comparative analysis of these two categories based on the type of encoder architecture. We assess the performance of the studied models on three real citation networks, which are characterized as attributed networks. For a more precise evaluation, we use NMI, ARI, and F1-measure as evaluation metrics. Additionally, we examine the running time efficiency of each model based on epochs. The results indicate that using advanced GNN decoders to reconstruct additional information, rather than just the topology, can significantly improve model performance. Additionally, employing a dual encoder with extra input information about modularity further enhances the performance. However, efficiency analysis shows that using advanced decoders with additional inputs for different types of reconstruction in the dual encoder architecture may increase running time. Despite this, the overall performance improvements justify the additional computational cost.

articleTitle: New Approaches of Progressive and Ensemble Deep Transfer Learning for Brain Tumor Classification in MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Early detection of brain tumors is of paramount importance to ensure effective care, increase the chances of cure and reduce treatment time. Thanks to technological advances in medical imaging, such as MRI, it is now possible to detect brain tumors and identify abnormalities by examining the shape, size and location of suspect tissues by a healthcare practitioner, requiring tedious work and a great deal of experience. The latter is often not easy to ensure. For this reason, the automation of this task using artificial intelligence is becoming more than a necessity. Using the concept of ensemble deep learning and convolutional neural networks, artificial intelligence enables the rapid and accurate interpretation of a large number of images, even those that present certain challenges and complexities. This paper presents approaches based on the combination and complementarity of several pre-trained CNN models, including VGG16, Densenet121, Xception, Inception and Resnet. In this context, several combination methods have been developed: bagging, stacking, bagging-stacking and progressive stacking combination. These approaches make it possible to pool the capabilities of each brain tumor classification model by combining the predictions of different models. Experimental results demonstrate the power and efficiency of this strategy.

articleTitle: Enhanced Cardiac Disease Detection Using MFCC Feature Extraction from PCG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Heart disease continues to be a major global health concern, necessitating rapid and accurate diagnosis. Traditional methods, such as stethoscope-based auscultation, encounter challenges in differentiating complex heart sounds. To tackle this issue, we introduce an innovative approach that integrates signal processing and deep learning techniques to analyze phonocardiogram (PCG) signals. The proposed framework involves categorizing, segmenting, sub-sampling PCG signals, and converting them into image representations using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC). A convolutional neural network (CNN) is employed to classify these images, achieving remarkable results with training accuracy of 99.60% and a validation accuracy of 99.51%, along with minimal loss rates of 0.0099 and 0.035 for training and validation, respectively. During the final testing phase, our model achieved an accuracy of 99.51%, precision of 99.51%, recall of 99.50%, F1-score 99.50% and a loss value of 0.035, underscoring the robustness of our methodology.
