This research underscores the potential of advanced signal processing and deep learning techniques to significantly enhance the accuracy and efficiency of heart disease diagnostics.

articleTitle: Federated Learning-Based Intelligent Indoor Smoke and Fire Detection System for Smart Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Ensuring safety in smart buildings is crucial due to the increasing prevalence of smoke and fire hazards in modern environments. This paper introduces a novel privacy-preserving FL approach based on a CNN1D for smoke and fire detection in smart buildings. Our system integrates data from wearable environmental sensors to train a lightweight, edge-deployable DL-CNN1D model, ensuring data privacy while enabling collaborative learning across distributed clients using Federated Averaging (FedAvg) aggregation. Experiments conducted on a comprehensive air measurement dataset for smoke and fire detection demonstrate exceptional performance, with the global model achieving 99.97% accuracy, 99.96% precision, in smoke and fire recognition. Our model demonstrates a low communication cost of 0.4 MB, underscoring its efficiency for real-time applications. Our FL-based approach represents a significant step towards balancing the need for robust safety systems with growing privacy concerns in smart building environments.

articleTitle: EEG Classification Using Contrastive Learning and Riemannian Tangent Space Representations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel advanced framework for the classification of Electroencephalography (EEG) signals through the integration of Riemannian geometry and a bespoke contrastive learning framework. Initially, the EEG signals are segmented and converted into covariance matrices, which are regularized to ensure positive definiteness, thus enabling their interpretation as Symmetric Positive Definite (SPD) matrices. These SPD matrices are then projected onto the Riemannian manifold, facilitating the extraction of discriminative features by utilizing Euclidean geometric operations within the tangent space. A specialized neural network architecture, TangentSpaceNet, is devised to map these features into a lower-dimensional space. In this space, a customized contrastive loss function, predicated on Euclidean distance, is implemented to enhance class separability. This approach substantially improves the robustness and accuracy of EEG signal classification. Empirical assessments highlight the effectiveness of the suggested approach, showcasing significant improvements in classifying performance 93% accuracy, 94%precision, 94% recall, and 94% F1-score. The novel fusion of Riemannian geometry and contrastive learning presents a sturdy and adaptable structure for analyzing EEG signals, presenting considerable prospects for utilization in brain-computer interfaces, cognitive neuroscience, and the identification of neurological conditions.

articleTitle: Enhancing EEG Signal Reconstruction in Cross-Domain Adaptation Using CycleGAN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper explores the applicability of CycleGAN, to reconstruct as well as improve brain-computer interface (BCI) signals. The experimental protocol used in the study involves a real-world table tennis dataset that includes multiple-channel high-density electroencephalography (EEG) data and structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans from individuals. The overall purpose is to develop a system that would allow enhancing the low-quality or partially damaged EEG signals by using information obtained from MRI, which is represented by Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT). This technique solves the problem of converting MRI data into effective EEG signals using CycleGAN. The approach may present some practical benefits in cases where signal quality becomes a problem, for example, in wireless or portable BCI equipment. Data preprocessing involves channel filtering of the data, segmentation, and conversion of the data to continuous wavelet transform format to be used by the model. This paper compares three models of CycleGAN, focusing on the various losses and using identity loss to improve them.

articleTitle: MobileViT architecture for Facial Beauty Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Facial beauty prediction is a complex task that involves quantifying human facial attractiveness based on visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel approach utilizing the MobileViT architecture, a hybrid model that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs) to tackle this challenge. The MobileViT model is specifically designed to capture both local details and global context, making it highly effective for facial image analysis while ensuring computational efficiency. We evaluated the performance of our model on the SCUT-FBP5500 dataset, a large-scale facial beauty dataset comprising 5,500 images labeled with beauty scores. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art results, demonstrating a Pearson correlation of 0.9515. These results significantly surpass those of existing methods, including CNN-based and semi-supervised approaches. The lightweight and efficient design of MobileViT renders it suitable for real-time applications on mobile and edge devices, highlighting its potential for practical use in beauty prediction tasks.

articleTitle: Improving Pretrained YAMNet for Enhanced Speech Command Detection via Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: This work addresses the need for enhanced accuracy and efficiency in speech command recognition systems, a critical component for improving user interaction in various smart applications. Leveraging the robust pretrained YAMNet model and transfer learning, this study develops a method that significantly improves speech command recognition. We adapt and train a YAMNet deep learning model to effectively detect and interpret speech commands from audio signals. Using the extensively annotated Speech Commands dataset (speech_commands_v0.01), our approach demonstrates the practical application of transfer learning to accurately recognize a predefined set of speech commands. The dataset is meticulously augmented, and features are strategically extracted to boost model performance. As a result, the final model achieved a recognition accuracy of 95.28%, underscoring the impact of advanced machine learning techniques on speech command recognition.This achievement marks substantial progress in audio processing technologies and establishes a new benchmark for future research in the field.

articleTitle: Thermal Imaging and Deep Learning For Neuropathy Risk Detection in Diabetic Feet
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Diabetic foot complications pose significant health risks, leading to infections and amputations. Early detection is crucial for effective management. This study utilizes thermal imaging technology to analyze temperature differences between feet as an early indicator of complications. Focusing on three parameters—overall thermal pattern, average temperature, and inter-foot temperature difference—we identified significant distinctions among three groups: Control, Diabetic Non-Neuropathic, and Diabetic Neuropathic patients. A novel plantar thermogram database was created from thermal images collected in Annaba, Algeria, contributing valuable region-specific data. Additionally, a user-friendly web application was developed to facilitate the analysis of thermal images, improving accessibility for healthcare professionals and enhancing patient care.

articleTitle: Fingerprint Recognition Improvement Using BSIF Features and KNN Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: Fingerprint recognition involves techniques for identifying individuals or verifying their identity based on unique fingerprint patterns. In recent years, it has become a popular area of research and plays a crucial role in personal identification. However, existing methods often require complex systems and have limitations in terms of accuracy. To overcome these issues, this paper presents a fingerprint recognition method that combines image enhancement, feature extraction using Binarized Statistical Image Features (BSIF), and classification with the k-nearest neighbors (KNN) algorithm. Initially, histogram equalization is employed in the image preprocessing stage to improve the quality of the fingerprint data, leading to more effective feature extraction. The Chikkerur approach is then employed for further image enhancement, followed by Region of Interest (ROI) extraction through the Singular Points method, which enhances the accuracy of feature representation. BSIF descriptors are subsequently extracted from the ROI to generate fingerprint features. Finally, the KNN classifier is implemented based on various distance metrics to optimize performance. The proposed approach was evaluated on the FVC 2002 DB1 Database, a widely recognized benchmark for fingerprint recognition. he results indicate that the proposed method, evaluated using the city block distance metric, outperforms state-of-the-art techniques, achieving a fingerprint identification accuracy of 95.25%.

articleTitle: ECG signal denoising based on optimal level and threshold selection in wavelet decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Telecommunications and Intelligent Systems (ICTIS)
abstract: White Gaussian Noise (WGN) significantly obscures critical features in Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, impeding the accurate diagnosis of cardiac abnormalities. This study introduces a novel denoising approach that integrates Wavelet Transform (WT) with a Genetic Algorithm (GA). WT decomposes the ECG signal into various frequency components, while GA, inspired by natural selection principles, optimizes the decomposition level and threshold values to efficiently eliminate WGN. Performance evaluation using the MIT-BIH database, with Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and Mean Squared Error (MSE) as metrics, demonstrates the efficiency of the proposed method. At an input SNR of 10 dB, the approach achieved an output SNR of 20.35 dB and an MSE of 0.0013, confirming its capability in significantly reducing noise and enhancing the clarity of ECG signals for improved diagnostic applications.
